scope: Read-only independent inspection of the exact final exported mesh and source snapshot, supplied reference photographs, CPU comparison images, and static functional-wing-pose evidence. No source changes or new render jobs.
improvements: The four-jet carrier is a shallow straight-run shelf rather than the previous thick oval.
The white rear bridge has genuine outboard depth concavity plus a carbon underside return.
The wing has swept/tapered chord, thin closed endplates, and curved carbon supports without the old detached box towers.
The front central windshield is a genuine single raked plane; roof and outboard glass retain their separate outlines.
The closed diffuser backing now has real per-channel depth rather than one flat door.

supportCapTriangulation.note: Concave outline is ear-clipped, not filled with an unsafe vertex-zero fan. Each side cap area equals the polygon area and outward face normals agree.

allExportedMeshes.note: The car uses intentional surface assemblies. Closed edited solids were checked as manifolds; that is not a claim that every exterior skin forms one global watertight solid.

rearRaySemanticReview.reason: The old first-hit z>=2.1 assertion described the old flat bulkhead. The intentional new channel front skin ranges z=2.0025..2.1475, so a hit between2.00 and2.10 is not a daylight hole.
requiredCompanionChecks: All welded backing edges have two opposite incident triangle edges.
Zero degenerate triangles and positive bounded volume.
The nearest hit is the intended channel skin, not the back cap.
All other ray-target meshes keep the prior2.1 depth requirement.
rearRaySemanticReview.recommendedExtraDiscriminator: For interior channel rays, faceIndex<1152 identifies the original12x48x2 front grid triangles. Boundary side-wall hits should be identified separately.

functionalPoseEvidence.exactFirstPassToFinalComparison: Only referenceClosedDiffuserBacking differs; all other exported meshes are semantically equal after material UUID normalization, including all ten active wing meshes.
functionalPoseEvidence.limit: These are exact static target-transform checks. They do not by themselves verify live driving interpolation, mechanical support anchoring through every intermediate pose, or browser/GPU rendering. First-pass whole-car pose images retain the first-pass diffuser backing.

reviewedRuntimeEvidence.note: Reviewed existing production-scene ray result and matching source hashes; not independently rerun as part of this review.

remainingLikenessLimits: Reference photograph cameras, exposure and lighting are unknown. No exact silhouette or dimensional-match claim is justified from these uncalibrated views.
The candidate carrier remains a regular rounded rectangle, and the tail lamp surround/registration pad remain comparatively rectilinear. The reference has subtler tapered/chamfered transitions.

The white bridge shows stronger localized studio highlights and the diffuser remains visually dark at16CPU samples. Material translation and lighting account for part of the apparent difference; those images cannot establish material identity.

The side-photo wing is in a raised, pitched state, while the canonical comparisons use the construction pose. Compare it with the separate air-brake evidence, not by baking a permanent pitch into the mesh.

No obvious daylight hole or inverted edited surface is visible in the inspected CPU views, but that observation is bounded to these cameras and supported closed-solid checks rather than a universal visibility proof.
action: No further redesign requested or performed. Candidate is suitable for parent review with the stated caveats.
